messages:
Ada: quick scan this morning of epilogue fusion opportunities for QKV packing + bias/rope. found two hotspots on A100 when seq <= 64 — epilogue writeback and a scalar exp/softmax tail.
Ryan: can you paste the profile? which metric points to writeback being the hotspot?
Ada: perf summary: for fused-attn v2 (no epilogue fuse) on 8k batch tokens: kernel time 3.2ms. with a minimal epilogue-fuse prototype it's 2.15ms (~33% lower) but L2 evict rate spikes on small batches. top counters: l2_read_miss_up=1.8x, l2_write_evict=2.6x, shared_load_latency up 15%.
Marta: that matches what I saw last week. epilogue fusion reduces global mem stores but increases register pressure and spills for some layouts — causes more L2 churn on paged-kv patterns.
Ada: exact flame: epilogue.gather_store (24%) + softmax_scalar_tail (18%). QKV packing moves some mem ops earlier so full fusion helps vectorize, but rope/bias inlining creates extra adds in epilogue path.
Ryan: interesting. so perf win for big batches but small-batch regression due to cache thrash. could we make selector choose fused-epilogue only when batch_tokens >= X or when running on card with L2>xx?
Marta: yes. propose heuristic: fused_epilogue_enabled if (avg_batch_tokens >= 4096 AND seq <= 64) OR (seq >= 256). also add runtime probe: run 3 microbatches with fused on warmup and measure l2_bw; fall back if evict_rate > threshold.
perf-bot: perf-runner #562 completed: fused-epilogue probe on a100x4 — avg kernel 2.2ms, evict_rate 2.4x
Ada: prototype selector patch: ```
selector:
  fused_epilogue:
    min_tokens: 4096
    max_seq: 64
    probe_runs: 3
    evict_threshold: 2.0
```
Ryan: looks good. also think about batcher changes: prefer packing microbatches with sticky-prefix caching so fused epilogue sees denser memory layout. small change: group requests by seq into same kernel launch more aggressively.
Marta: +1. another idea: split epilogue into two variants at compile time — low-reg (no rope inline) and high-reg (rope/bias fused). selector picks variant based on register pressure estimate from kernel metadata.
Ada: compiled low-reg reduces spills but loses some vectorization; measured: low-reg fused gives 2.6ms, high-reg fused 2.15ms when it fits. cost tradeoff is clear.
Ryan: action items: (1) land selector probe and config (Ada), (2) add batcher affinity by seq (Marta), (3) run 24h smoke on canary infra with perf logging (me). I'll open PRs and bench jobs.
Marta: I'll also add a microbenchmark for paged-KV eviction scenario so we can tune evict_threshold empirically.
Ada: thanks. tagging @perf-bot when jobs start. want to avoid surprise regressions during next release. :eyes:
perf-bot: perf-runner: scheduled nightly job 563 for fused-epilogue canary.
Ryan: nice. keep notes here with short perf snaps (kernel ms, evict_ratio, spills) so we have a quick regression signal.
Ada: will do. saving current probe results to /tmp/fuse-scan-1939998888.log and attaching to PR.
Marta: cool. I'll try a small compile tweak that reduces register usage for rope math and report back tomorrow.
Ada: perfect — thanks everyone.
